name: Stomach vacuum / waist training

lead: The stomach vacuum is an exercise in which the abdomen is drawn inward, aimed at the transversus abdominis, the deepest of the four front abdominal wall muscles. Users practice it for a tighter abdominal wall and a smaller-looking waist that supports a V-taper.

The muscle is well described anatomically, but evidence on this use is thin: a looksmax.org thread has a user reporting he nearly lost the ability to do it and regained it with renewed training. Wikipedia notes it is disputed whether training this deep core muscle specifically is worthwhile, and a 2011 study found abdominal exercise alone does not reduce abdominal fat or girth.

paras: People practice it as a hold, drawing the belly in toward the spine, usually fitted into a warm-up or daily routine alongside regular training and fat loss. Waist training is sometimes also used for compression garments, which this entry does not cover.
No harms data were found for the exercise itself.

angle.text: Users practice the stomach vacuum to train the transversus abdominis and make the waist look smaller, supporting a V-taper. The muscle is well described anatomically. Research on this use is thin, and abdominal exercise alone does not reduce belly fat or girth according to a 2011 study.

lead: The stomach vacuum is an abdominal exercise in which the stomach is pulled inward, discussed in looksmaxxing as a way to make the waist look smaller. It is associated with the transversus abdominis, the deepest of the four muscles of the front abdominal wall [1].

Community material is limited to short forum posts, such as a thread in which a user says he nearly lost the ability to perform it two years earlier and can do it easily again after resuming training [2]. No clinical studies were found.

paras: Wikipedia's abdominal exercise article describes the transversus abdominis as part of the abdominal wall and says focused training of this deep core muscle is disputed, with some experts recommending broader regimens [1].

The same article states that whether abdominal exercise reduces belly fat is highly disputed, citing a 2011 study that found abdominal exercises alone are not enough to reduce abdominal fat and girth. It adds that reducing fat requires an energy deficit [1].

lore.intro: Discussion on looksmax.org is brief and anecdotal [2].

claims.claim: The stomach vacuum skill can be lost and regained with training.
